status.label: Reproduce redirected-folder installation
status.detail: The per-user installer fails with a cross-drive Roaming junction; a later release changed the failure to a silent exit rather than confirming a fix.

next_action.label: Compare junction and ordinary-profile installs
next_action.reason: The report already supplies scope, folder shape, screenshots and a historical installer log.

reproduce.title: Compare per-user installation with ordinary and redirected Roaming folders
reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable per-user installer first; 0.76.1 original and 0.82.0-era changed failure as historical controls
prerequisites: Disposable Windows VM/account snapshot with a second local NTFS volume and sufficient space.
Do not redirect an active user's Roaming directory or change a production profile.
Obtain the existing report's public installer log before interpreting any new trace.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare two disposable Windows test profiles from a clean snapshot: an ordinary local Roaming directory and a non-destructive fixture whose Roaming junction points to an accessible directory on a second local NTFS volume. Preserve identical directory permissions and record how to restore the snapshot. Do not alter the signed-in production profile or use a network drive as a substitute for the reported local junction.
steps: Install the same per-user package under the ordinary profile and record successful component and known-folder resolution.
Repeat under the cross-volume Roaming-junction profile using the same user scope and account privileges; capture installer transaction logs and the first failing action.
Compare unelevated and elevated launches only as controls; do not assume elevation fixes a missing path because the author already tried it.
Check whether the latest build still fails or exits silently, and separate the first path-validation/component failure from a downstream rollback.
If reproducing historical builds, compare the 0.82.0-era behavior that the reporter says changed from an error to silent exit.
reproduce.expected_result: Installation succeeds when the user's known-folder target is accessible through a valid local junction. Any unsupported case returns a diagnostic error rather than silently exiting.

actions.label: Approve redirected-folder installer investigation
actions.note: Conditional plan; identify the current failing installer action before modifying setup.

judgment.rationale: A clear local junction prerequisite, per-user scope and historical log enable maintainer reproduction. The later silent exit is unresolved, not evidence of a fix.
evidence: The report specifies a cross-drive AppData Roaming junction, per-user installer and failure even when elevated.
The author says the 0.82.0-era installer now exits silently: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/30294#issuecomment-2241068906
#32780 is closed as a duplicate, but its mapped-network-drive folder-redirection setup differs from the original local junction.
judgment.recommended_action: Use an isolated per-user junction fixture to identify the first failing setup action before approving a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: A setup path-resolution/component-destination correction is applicable if the junction failure persists. The cited release-note improvement did not resolve the reporter's failure, and no directly covering fixing PR was identified.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve accessible redirected user folders without silent installer failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a per-user installer action validates or constructs a component destination using an unresolved/unavailable Roaming path instead of the accessible junction target. The exact action and any later DSC component involvement remain unconfirmed.
plan: Compare current per-user installer traces for ordinary and cross-volume-junction profiles, starting from the existing log and identifying the first failure rather than the final rollback code.

Locate the failing known-folder/destination-resolution action in the current installer tree; resolve the supported user-folder target consistently and validate accessibility in the actual install context without rewriting user junctions.
Ensure a failure preserves a useful installer diagnostic instead of silent exit; keep mapped network drives and unsupported/unavailable targets as separate tested cases.
Add integration regression coverage for per-user local cross-volume junctions and verify normal per-machine/per-user installs are unchanged.
verification: A valid accessible local Roaming junction installs and upgrades successfully without modifying the junction.
Ordinary profiles still install; unavailable or permission-denied targets fail clearly and roll back cleanly.
Confirm current behavior separately from the historical 0.82.0 release-note claim.

confidence.rationale: The folder-shape dependency is specific and reproducible, but no current installer action has yet been traced.

issue_context.summary: Per-user PowerToys installation regressed when Roaming is a junction to another local drive. A later installer stopped showing the error but still did not complete.
known_information: Original 0.76.1 report includes screenshots, a bootstrapper/MSI log and explicit per-user scope.
Elevation was already tried without success.
The 0.82.0-era follow-up says silent exit, not successful installation.
The live issue is open and unassigned; duplicate #32780 concerns mapped-drive redirection.
inferences: Known-folder resolution or install-context access is plausible; neither DSC nor permissions is proven as the root cause.
Mapped-drive and local-junction failures may share setup handling but require separate controls.
issue_context.analysis: Do not request installer scope or generic logs already supplied. Reproduce the exact local-junction shape in an isolated profile and distinguish the current first failure before modifying installer behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the full report, its release-note follow-up and public timeline.
Read #32780, including its explicit duplicate closure and different all-users/network-drive setup.
A direct issue-number PR search found no concrete covering fix; the release-note quotation is not an issue-resolution claim.
No installer execution or attachment-log root-cause analysis was performed in this pass.

information_gaps.information: First failing action in a current per-user installer run under the exact accessible local-junction fixture.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates obsolete DSC behavior, current destination resolution and unrelated network-drive access failures.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer compares transaction logs from the disposable ordinary/junction profiles above, first consulting the already attached historical log.
